The article stated that this description was odd because Bush had already answered one question about his brother, and was insensitive to those who proudly served and believed in the cause. Later, co-moderator Chris Wallace also asked Bush a question in which he referred to "your father and your brother."

The New York Post reported Thursday that Jeffrey Corzine, the youngest of former New Jersey Gov. Jon Corzine's three children, was found dead from an apparent suicide in a Mexico City hotel. Sources told The Post that Corzine killed himself in the hotel. The Post also reported that Jeffrey Corzine was described as depressed and had been drinking heavily recently. According to previous statements from his family, he was thought to have been "clean" and "doing well" until now. Sources said the younger Corzine had a history of substance-abuse problems and had been in and out of rehab. Sources said he had been living in California and working as a drug counselor and had appeared to have turned his life around.

On Tuesday, former President Bill Clinton appeared on CBS's "The Late Show" and addressed an earlier appearance on NBC's "Today." During the interview, Clinton said he did not owe former White House intern Monica Lewinsky an apology for inappropriate sexual conduct. He said: "When I saw the interview, I thought that — because they had to, you know, distill it. It looked like I was saying that I didn't apologize and I had no intention to. And I was mad at me." He continued: "It wasn't my finest hour. I meant it then; I mean it now. I've had to live with the consequences every day since." Clinton added: "I still believe this #MeToo movement is long overdue, necessary, and should be supported."

On Sunday, Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appeared on CBS' "Face the Nation." He said he was "baffled" by the White House's criticisms of Israeli settlements because "ethnic purification" goes "against the American values." Last week, after a Jewish group announced that settlers were moving into several apartment buildings purchased in a predominantly Arab neighborhood in Jerusalem, the White House said the move is "poisoning" the peace process. Netanyahu said that putting any restrictions on where Jews could live is "against the American values. And it doesn't bode well for peace." He said not allowing Jews and Arabs to live together is promoting "ethnic purification." He added: "The idea that we'd have this ethnic purification as a condition for peace, I think it's anti-peace."

Sen. Tom Cotton (R-AR) denounced the Iranian nuclear deal that President Obama praised early Tuesday morning, calling it a mistake. In an interview on MSNBC's Morning Joe, Cotton said, "This proposed deal is a terrible dangerous mistake that's going to pave the path for Iran to get a nuclear weapon while giving them tens of billions of dollars of sanctions relief." Cotton, a freshman senator, has made his opposition to the deal the center of his political career. He described Iran as an "outlaw, terrorist sponsoring, anti-American regime" and criticized the deal for leaving its nuclear program intact. Cotton said he believed Congress would oppose the deal once the full details of the deal were released, including provisions such as lifting the arms embargo on Iran and the weakness of requirements for nuclear inspections. "The American people will repudiate this and I believe Congress will kill the deal," he stated.

Iran's official IRNA news agency reported Tuesday that Kavous Seyed-Emami, a dual Iranian and Canadian citizen, was in custody for passing information on the country's missile bases to the CIA and Mossad and planning to create an environmental crisis. IRNA quotes Tehran prosecutor Abbas Jafari Dolatabdi as saying Seyed-Emami and a network of people installed cameras in strategic areas of the country pretending to observe environmental issues but, in fact, were sending images and information to foreigners. Dolatabdi said Seyed-Emami hosted one of two U.S. intelligence officers during their visit to Iran. He did not elaborate. On Monday, Iran said Seyed-Emami took his own life.

Donald Trump Jr. said that if his father loses to Hillary Clinton in Tuesday's presidential election, the Republican nominee would concede defeat if things are "legit and fair." On MSNBC's "Morning Joe," when asked if his father would concede defeat in the event of a "clear cut" win for Mrs. Clinton, Donald Trump Jr. said, "Of course — all we've wanted is a fair fight." He added, "If he loses and it's legit and fair, and there's not obvious stuff out there — without question, yes." During the third presidential debate, Donald Trump said he would keep people in suspense as to whether he would accept the results of the election. He later said he would accept the results if he won.

Republican presidential candidate Dr. Ben Carson canceled all remaining campaign events and traveled to Omaha, Nebraska, to be with the family during the incident. The campaign issued a press release saying three campaign volunteers and one campaign employee were involved in a car accident in Iowa on Tuesday. The release said a van transporting three campaign volunteers and a campaign employee hit a patch of ice and flipped on its side before being struck by another vehicle. Three passengers, including the campaign staffer driving, were checked out at Cass County Memorial Hospital in Atlantic, Iowa, and one volunteer was transported to the trauma center at the University of Nebraska Medical Center in Omaha, Nebraska. The campaign said Carson had spoken with the attending physician and family of the volunteer being transported to Omaha. The press release said Carson had cancelled all remaining campaign events and would travel to Omaha this afternoon to be with the family during the difficult time.

President Trump said Wednesday that a New York Times report showing he lost more than $1 billion from 1985 to 1994 does not accurately depict real estate practices during that time frame. Trump tweeted: "Real estate developers in the 1980's & 1990's, more than 30 years ago, were entitled to massive write offs and depreciation which would, if one was actively building, show losses and tax losses in almost all cases. Much was non monetary. Sometimes considered 'tax shelter,' you would get it by building, or even buying." He added: "You always wanted to show losses for tax purposes....almost all real estate developers did - and often re-negotiate with banks, it was sport. Additionally, the very old information put out is a highly inaccurate Fake News hit job."

Melania Trump broke ground on a White House tennis pavilion funded by private donations. The White House said Tuesday that the pavilion is fueled by Mrs. Trump's respect for classical architecture and passion to provide a functional recreational area for all First Families. The White House said the pavilion uses the historic Children's Garden, compliments the architecture of the Executive Mansion, and draws on inspiration from both the East and West wings. Mrs. Trump said: "As we break ground on the new tennis pavilion, it is a great honor to share this moment alongside the many talented individuals and craftsmen involved in bringing it to fruition. Architectural inspiration for the pavilion is drawn from the White House, with the end goal of the new structure on the south lawn complementing and contributing to the People's house. It is my hope that this private space will function as a place to gather and spend leisure time for First Families."

American passengers from the Diamond Princess cruise ship docked in Japan, on which about 400 cases of the coronavirus have been confirmed, will be flown to two military bases in the United States, Department of Defense officials confirmed Sunday. The U.S. State Department has chartered two flights to evacuate some passengers aboard the ship. One flight will land at Travis Air Force Base in northern California while the other will be taken to Lackland Air Force Base in San Antonio, Texas. The American passengers will be subjected to a mandatory 14-day quarantine period managed by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control after arrival. Should any of the evacuees test positive or become symptomatic with the coronavirus, they will be transferred to a "suitable" off base medical facility, Department of Defense officials said.

Sen. Pat Roberts apologized Thursday after receiving backlash for a joke he made about mammograms while discussing the Republicans' plan to repeal and replace Obamacare. A Talking Points Memo reporter asked the Kansas Republican if he supports a potential change in the GOP's plan that would scrap Obamacare's Essential Health Benefits rule, which requires insurers to cover "essential" health services like maternity care and mammograms. He said in a statement that he knows "several individuals whose lives have been saved by mammograms" and understands their importance, CNN reported. Before he issued his apology Thursday, Roberts told CNN that he does not think all of the benefits declared "essential" are really necessary, and that people should be able to choose plans that cater to what they think is essential. Asked whether mammograms should be covered, Roberts suggested he would not need them because he is a man, CNN reported.

Additionally, the very old information put out is a highly inaccurate Fake News hit job."

Former CIA director John Brennan tweeted on Friday that President Trump's presidency is "collapsing." Brennan wrote: "Your kakistocracy is collapsing after its lamentable journey. As the greatest Nation history has known, we have the opportunity to emerge from this nightmare stronger & more committed to ensuring a better life for all Americans, including those you have so tragically deceived." A "kakistocracy" is defined as a system of government run by the worst, least qualified, or most unscrupulous citizens. Brennan was responding to Trump's criticisms of former FBI Director James Comey on Twitter, calling Comey an "untruthful slime ball who was, as time has proven, a terrible Director of the FBI." Comey is out with a new book that is highly critical of the president, who fired the FBI director a year ago.

Rep. Raul Labrador (R-ID) has officially entered the race for House Majority Leader and will face Rep. Kevin McCarthy (R-CA) for the chance to succeed Rep. Eric Cantor (R-VA), who lost his congressional primary this week and will step down by the end of July. Labrador's entry, reported by Politico, comes after Rep. Pete Sessions (R-TX) withdrew from the race, stating the need to avoid "division" in the Republican Party. House Conservatives had hoped to contest a major leadership office after Cantor's defeat by conservative Dave Brat, and after leadership elections in 2011 and 2013 did not elevate any Tea Party members to senior positions in the caucus. Labrador, who is Latino, is also an opponent of "comprehensive" immigration reform as passed by the Senate, which was a key issue in Cantor's primary, and withdrew from bipartisan talks last year.

On Wednesday on the Senate floor, Judiciary Committee member Sen. Jeff Flake (R-AZ) said he will oppose advancing any of President Donald Trump's judicial nominations out of committee until legislation protecting Department of Justice special counsel Robert Mueller receives a full Senate vote. Flake expressed concern for Mueller's Russian investigation after the appointment of Matthew Whitaker as acting Attorney General. After Majority Leader Mitch McConnell (R-KY) blocked a full vote, Flake said, "One further note on this unanimous consent that has just failed today. Senator Coons and I are prepared to make it again and again until there is a vote on this vital bipartisan legislation on the Senate floor. I have informed the majority leader that I will not vote to advance any of the 21 judicial nominees pending in the Judiciary Committee or vote to confirm the 32 judges awaiting confirmation on the Senate floor until S. 2644 is brought to the full Senate for a vote."

On Thursday, Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL) appeared on CNN's "Newsroom" and said President Donald Trump's attorney Rudy Giuliani had "lost his mind." Wasserman Schultz said Giuliani had "obstructed lawful policies and procedures as it relates to foreign policy, undermined the President's own staff, attempted to get the president of Ukraine to invest in the President's primary political opponent, and was involved in enabling the President to withhold foreign aid that Congress had appropriated and that he had signed into law." She added, "So if Rudy Giuliani thinks he should be praised for that type of activity, I think the history will shine a light and reflect quite differently."

President Donald Trump announced Wednesday that the United States would temporarily close the border with Canada to non-essential traffic amid the coronavirus crisis. "We will be, by mutual consent, temporarily closing our Northern Border with Canada to non-essential traffic," Trump wrote on Twitter. "Trade will not be affected. Details to follow!" Trump announced the border closure after CNN reported details of the discussions between the two countries. On Tuesday, Trump said he did not want to say he was considering closing the borders between Canada and Mexico. "We are discussing things with Canada and we're discussing things with Mexico, quite honestly, and again, the relationship is outstanding with both, outstanding," he said. Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau is following the lead of other countries by restricting entry during the coronavirus crisis. On Monday, he announced that Canada would close the country's borders to foreigners, with the exception of American citizens.

South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham called Republican frontrunner Donald Trump a "jackass" during a Tuesday press conference. Trump read out Graham's private cell phone number live. Graham told CBS This Morning: "I don't care if he drops out. Stay in the race, just stop being a jackass. The world is falling apart. We're becoming Greece. The Ayatollah's on the verge of having a nuclear weapon, and you're slandering everybody and anybody to stay in the news. You know, run for president, but don't be the world's biggest jackass."

On June 9 Virginia state senator Phillip Pucket (D-Russel) resigned his seat, giving Republicans control of the legislative body and giving him the opportunity for a position on the state tobacco commission and his daughter the chance for a judgeship. Slate reported the resignation effectively marks the end of Governor Terry McAuliffe's (D) plan to expand Medicaid under Obamacare. The senate was split between 20 Democrats and 20 Republicans prior to June 9. According to The Washington Post, Democrats said Republicans were trying to buy the senate with job offers in order to thwart what McAuliffe said would be an expansion of health care coverage to 400,000 low-income Virginians. Delegate Scott A. Surovell (D-Fairfax) said he was astounded that the Republicans "will do anything and everything to prevent low-income Virginians from getting health care." He referred to Republicans as "bullies" and said he hopes McAuliffe will continue standing up to them.

Former Michigan congressman and chairman of the House Intelligence Committee Pete Hoekstra spoke with Breitbart News Daily SiriusXM host Alex Marlow on Wednesday regarding FBI Director James Comey and NSA Director Adm. Michael Rogers' testimony before the House Intelligence Committee. Hoekstra said he found it very interesting that Comey rules, that he arbitrarily decides what investigations can be made public and which ones cannot be made public. Hoekstra called it "amazing," adding, "the leaks thing is the one area where we know that crimes have been committed, felonies have been committed, and he can't commit to say that there's actually investigations going on in that area." Breitbart News Daily airs on SiriusXM Patriot 125 weekdays from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. Eastern.

President Obama tweeted support for a high school student arrested in Irving, Texas, after he brought a homemade clock to school. The student, Ahmen Mohamed, was called to the principal's office after a teacher reported it. Police arrested him, put him in handcuffs, and took his fingerprints. Obama said, "Cool clock, Ahmed. Want to bring it to the White House? We should inspire more kids like you to like science. It's what makes America great." The school suspended Mohamed for three days. Irving Police Chief Larry Boyd defended the decision to arrest Mohamed on the grounds that it was "a hoax bomb" but said that it was a "naive accident." Boyd said, "We are confident it's not an explosive device," confirming that all charges were dropped.

In Massachusetts, the race for the late Senator Edward M. Kennedy's Senate seat is breaking in favor of the Republicans on the eve of the election. Democrat Martha Coakley is trailing Republican Scott Brown. Coakley has leaned on President Obama this weekend to try to catch up to Brown. The momentum for Brown is clearly with Brown heading into the home stretch. The energy and enthusiasm is with Brown as independents are breaking 2-1 for the Republican and Democrats appear to be giving up 20% of their own votes to Brown. This is no surprise given the election landscape this year as voters are fed up with the spending by Congress. Such spending is epitomized by the health care bill Congress is trying to push through before seating Brown if he is elected. Doug Schoen is a Fox News contributor, pollster and author of "The Political Fix." (Henry Holt).

Pennsylvania State Police said Sunday that 20-year-old Andrew Joseph Todd of Mount Bethel, Pennsylvania, was shot and killed when he refused officers' orders to drop his weapon inside the Walmart late Saturday. Police were dispatched to the store shortly after 10 p.m. Saturday on reports of an armed man threatening and pointing a weapon at customers. Officials said about 100 people were in the store at the time. State police said officers ordered Todd to drop his weapon. He refused and continued to point it at officers. Police then fired at Todd, striking him in the upper chest. Todd was transported to Pocono Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead by the Monroe County coroner. State police said no customers or officers were injured. The Pocono Record reported Todd was carrying two guns and a machete.

Former New York Gov. George Pataki, who dropped out of the presidential race a few weeks ago, endorsed Marco Rubio for president on Tuesday. In an interview with Fox News, the former Republican governor said Rubio could bring Americans together. "In my mind there's one person who stands out, and that is Senator Marco Rubio," Pataki said. "Senator Rubio has the leadership, he has the vision, he has the intelligence from Congress to understand what it takes to defend us from radical Islam. I'm proud to endorse Senator Rubio." The endorsement follows another former presidential candidate, former Texas Gov. Rick Perry, who endorsed Texas Sen. Ted Cruz. Pataki dropped out of the race last month after failing to gain traction in the GOP primary. His Rubio endorsement comes less than a week before the Iowa caucuses; polls in the state show Rubio in third place, behind Donald Trump and Cruz.

On Monday, former Trump aide Omarosa Manigault Newman appeared on ABC's "The View." Co-host Joy Behar asked Manigault Newman whether she had the N-word on tape. Manigault Newman said she did not hold the tape but had heard the tape. She said they had been talking about releasing it and were suspecting they would release it around the midterm elections. Behar said, "That won't hurt him. That will not hurt him." Manigault Newman said, "The Trump world cult will probably applaud when they hear him say it because they're desensitized to his racist ways."

The U.S. Senate voted 49-49 Wednesday to confirm Kansas Gov. Sam Brownback's nomination for ambassador's post. Vice President Mike Pence broke the tie in Brownback's favor. The vote ended debate on Brownback's nomination by President Donald Trump to be U.S. ambassador-at-large for international religious freedom. The action starts a 30-hour clock on holding a final vote, though it could come sooner. Trump first nominated Brownback for the ambassador's post in July. Democrats and LGBT groups opposed his appointment. In 2015, Brownback rescinded an executive order from a previous Democratic governor banning discrimination in state hiring and employment against LGBT individuals. Brownback would resign as governor if confirmed. Republican Lt. Gov. Jeff Colyer would be elevated to governor.

The Pentagon will review new Army hairstyle regulations after lawmakers criticized them as discriminatory toward women of color. Pentagon spokesman Rear Adm. John Kirby said Tuesday that Defense Secretary Chuck Hagel has directed his deputy secretary to work with service chiefs to address the concerns about the new standards. The standards include bans on most twists, dreadlocks and large cornrows, all styles used predominantly by black women with natural hairstyles. Sixteen female members of the Congressional Black Caucus sent a letter to the Pentagon earlier this month stating the changes unfairly restrict the hairstyles of women of color. The letter stated: "Though we understand the intent of the updated regulation is to ensure uniformity in our military, it is seen as discriminatory rules targeting soldiers who are women of color with little regard to what is needed to maintain their natural hair." Kirby added that after the reviews are complete, Hagel will make "whatever appropriate adjustments to DOD policy are necessary."

Former U.S. President Bill Clinton spoke at the Clinton Global Initiative annual meeting Wednesday in New York. He said Russian President Vladimir Putin can be trusted and has never broken his word on a personal agreement between them. "He kept his word in all the deals we made," Clinton said. He also praised his daughter Chelsea, placing her above Hillary Clinton on the list of people he would make a good POTUS. Clinton said he believes his daughter Chelsea would be a better president than his wife, Hillary, "over the long run." "Day after tomorrow, my wife because she's had more experience. Over the long run, Chelsea. She knows more than we do about everything," Clinton said. "I feel like I'm going to school every day when we have conversations."

The self-described mastermind of the Sept. 11 attacks, Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, said in a statement filed in Manhattan federal court late Sunday that Sulaiman Abu Ghaith, an al-Qaida spokesman, had no role in planning military operations for al-Qaida. Mohammed said Abu Ghaith served as an al-Qaida spokesman because he was "an eloquent, spellbinding speaker." Mohammed said Abu Gaith "had nothing to do with military operations." Abu Gaith is a son-in-law of bin Laden and is charged with conspiring to kill Americans. Mohammed is in a detention facility in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. Abu Gaith's lawyers hope to use his testimony at the trial. They would need U.S. District Judge Lewis A. Kaplan's approval to introduce the information.

Rick Santorum endorsed Marco Rubio for president on Wednesday evening, hours after it was widely reported that he would drop out of the race. The former U.S. senator from Pennsylvania won the Iowa caucuses in 2012. Santorum made the endorsement in an appearance on Fox News Channel's "On the Record" show, where he formally announced the suspension of his campaign. Show host Greta Van Susteren tweeted out several statements about Rubio attributed to Santorum. Santorum's effort to repeat his 2012 run had not succeeded and never reached the low single-digit polling threshold. According to Van Susteren's Twitter account, Santorum said, "I don't endorse lightly."

During an interview with ABC's George Stephanopoulos, former FBI Director James Comey's wife, Patrice, said she supported Hillary Clinton and was "devastated" when Donald Trump won. "I wanted a woman president really badly, and I supported Hillary Clinton," Patrice Comey told Stephanopoulos. "A lot of my friends worked for her. And I was devastated when she lost." James Comey said his wife and girls marched in the Women's March the day after Trump's inauguration. "At least my four daughters — probably all five of my kids, wanted Hillary Clinton to be the first woman president. I know my amazing spouse did."

Sen. Ben Sasse, R-Neb., tweeted Tuesday that Sen. Jeff Flake's $100 check to Democrat Doug Jones to help him in the Alabama Senate race against Republican Roy Moore is a "bad idea." Sasse wrote: "This donation is a bad idea. It's possible to be against BOTH partial birth abortion AND child molestation. Happily, most Americans are." Moore faces several accusations of sexual impropriety with teenage girls when he was in his 30s. He denies the allegations. When a Twitter user asked for Sasse's solution to the Dec. 12 special election, the Nebraska senator replied: "Have said from day one I wouldn't vote for either of them. If you don't reject 2 bad choices now, you won't get better choices in the future."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday rejected a key aspect of President Obama's Middle East policy speech, saying that a return to his country's 1967 borders would spell disaster for the Jewish state. In a statement released late Thursday, Netanyahu called the 1967 lines "indefensible." The statement could set the stage for a tense meeting Friday when Netanyahu goes to the White House. In his speech, Obama said a future Palestinian state must be based in territories captured by Israel in the 1967 Mideast war, with minor adjustments reached through negotiations. Netanyahu said such a withdrawal would jeopardize Israel's security and leave major West Bank settlements outside Israeli borders.

President Obama will meet with weathermen from across the nation on Tuesday afternoon for what has been dubbed "Weather from the White House." The White House released a National Climate Assessment on Monday that predicts floods, droughts, superstorms and other near-apocalyptic scenarios. Obama will record the interviews Tuesday afternoon. The White House did not specifically state that climate change would be the focus of the interviews. NBC meteorologist Al Roker tweeted Monday: "I'm going to the White House to interview President Obama about the National Climate Assessment report coming out." The White House also said anchors will be granted special behind-the-scenes access to the president and his top advisers throughout the day.

U.S. Rep. Gabrielle Giffords and other victims of Saturday's shooting are being treated at University Medical Center in Tucson. The hospital fired three employees for accessing private patient medical records in violation of hospital policy, FoxNews.com confirmed. The hospital would not reveal the number or identities of patients who had their records accessed or whether any were victims of the shooting that left six people dead and 14 others wounded. Hospital spokeswoman Loretta McKenzie told FoxNews.com that the patients had been notified. In addition to the three clerical staff fired by the hospital, a contracted nurse was terminated. Giffords remained in critical condition after she was shot once in the head. She is expected to live and has been making progress, including making small movements on her own, tugging at her hospital gown and touching her wounds, one of her doctors said Wednesday. Her long-term outlook remains unclear.

Four years ago, President Obama beat Mitt Romney 51.5% to 46% in Colorado. Nine months ago, Clinton was tied or beating every Republican in Colorado. According to the latest Quinnipiac poll, to0day, every major Republican beats the former Secretary of State by double digits. The best poll in the swing state is 38%. Rubio leads Clinton 52% to 36 percent; Carson leads Clinton 52% to 38 percent; Cruz tops Clinton 51% to 38 percent. Only 34% of Colorado voters believes Hillary Clinton shares their values. In their respective primaries, Carson leads the Republicans with 25% support. Marco Rubio is in second place at 19%. Trump has fallen to third place with 17% support. In the same poll, back in March, Clinton was polling in the mod-forties and statistically tied with her Republican opponents.

U.S. Rep. Xochitl Torres Small of New Mexico said Wednesday she will not seek the Democratic nomination for an open U.S. Senate seat. Torres Small announced she will not run to replace retiring U.S. Sen. Tom Udall and will focus on the state's 2nd Congressional District. U.S. Rep. Ben Ray Lujan, the No. 4 ranked Democrat in Congress, said Monday he will run for the state's open U.S. Senate seat in 2020. Lujan is the first politician to declare his candidacy for the Senate seat. Democrats hope to keep their hold on the seat held by Udall, who announced last week that he will not seek a third term. Torres Small, a freshman, won the traditionally Republican district in November.

North Korea on Thursday demanded the end of U.N. sanctions as a condition for talks to continue with world leaders who have been trying to calm war-like rhetoric. A spokesman for the Policy Department of the National Defense Commission said the U.S.-South Korean military drills must end, too, CBS News reported. "Dialogue can never go with war actions," the statement read, as CBS reported. Other conditions, CBS reported: North Korea demanded the United States withdraw all nuclear weapon assets from the South. And South Korea must put a stop to all rhetoric critical of the North. South Korea immediately dismissed the demands. "We again strongly urge North Korea to stop this kind of insistence that we cannot totally understand and go down the path of a wise choice," a spokesman for the South Korean Foreign Ministry said in the CBS report. North Korea has been threatening to attack South Korea, Japan and the United States for weeks.

On Sunday, former CIA Director Mike Morell appeared on ABC's "This Week" and discussed his op-ed denouncing Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump and endorsing Hillary Clinton. Morell said he would trust Clinton with "the crown jewels" of the U.S. government. When asked why America should trust her to be commander-in-chief, Morell said, "I think there's a bigger issue here, right? I worked with her for four years. Very closely when she was secretary of state. I was at the CIA. I provided her personally provided her some of the most sensitive information that the Central Intelligence Agency has. She never misused it. Always protected it. I would trust her with the crown jewels of the United States government. And more importantly, I would trust her with the future security of the country and the future security of my kids."

The United States is providing nearly $25 million in additional humanitarian aid to help the Philippines deal with the devastation and deaths wrought by Typhoon Haiyan last month. U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry flew to the worst-hit central Tacloban city Wednesday and announced the additional food aid, shelter materials, water and other supplies for typhoon-lashed families after surveying battered villages and consoling survivors. The U.S. assistance package has reached $86 million with the new aid to one of its closest Asian allies. Washington's emergency aid is helping 3 million people in the hardest-hit regions, where the U.S. military has transported more than 2,495 tons of relief supplies and evacuated more than 21,000 survivors. Haiyan left more than 6,000 people dead and nearly 1,800 others missing.

Melania Trump's professional website has disappeared from the internet, as her educational background has come under scrutiny. Her site, which at one time featured her biography, now redirects users to a website for her husband Donald Trump's business, the Trump Organization, The Huffington Post reported. The disappearance of the website comes amid speculation over whether the former model and potential First Lady received her undergraduate degree in design and architecture from the University of Ljubljana in her native Slovenia. Melania's online biography claimed that she had received the college degree. An unauthorized book about her life called "Melania Trump: The Inside Story" alleged that she ditched school after one year to pursue a career in modeling. According to the Huffington Post, older versions of Melania's website in online archives, including one from 2012, claimed that she earned a degree in architecture and design from the university.

A WBUR poll released late Wednesday showed Harvard professor Elizabeth Warren leading Massachusetts Senator Scott Brown 45 percent to 40 percent among likely voters, with 12 percent undecided. Earlier in the week, three other polls also showed Warren leading Brown. A Suffolk University/WHDH News 7 poll had her ahead by 4 percent, a Public Policy Polling Survey had her up by 2 percent, and a poll commissioned by MassLive.com showed Brown leading by 6 percentage points. The two will face off Thursday night in the first of three debates scheduled before the November election. The WBUR poll was conducted Sept. 15-17 among 507 likely voters and has a 4.4 percent margin of error.

Israel and the United Nations warned the United States that Iran cannot be trusted outside of an agreement to halt uranium enrichment. Obama and his national security team counter that assessment. The administration is also working to avoid congressional opposition. According to the AP, prior to talks now underway, Secretary of State John Kerry and National Security Adviser Susan Rice appealed to Senators in a White House meeting to hold off on seeking additional sanctions to give Iran time to demonstrate Iran's seriousness in addressing concerns it is trying to develop nuclear weapons. Republican Senators are working to keep penalties in place and toughen them unless Iran freezes its nuclear program completely. Israel continues to maintain U.N. Security Council demands that Iran halt uranium enrichment as a prerequisite for serious talks or relief from sanctions.

On this week's broadcast of "Fox News Sunday," Rep. Adam Schiff (D-CA) reacted to Justice Department Inspector General Michael Horowitz's report on the launch of the FBI's Russia probe. Schiff said that had he known two years ago that the FBI was abusing the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), he would have called them out. Schiff said, "I'm certainly willing to admit that the inspector general found serious abuses of FISA that I was unaware of. Had I known of them, Chris, yes, I would have called out the FBI at the same time. But I think it's only fair to judge what we know at the time, not what would be revealed two years later, but yes, there were very serious abuses of the FISA process, they need to be corrected, we need to make sure they never happen again."

Federal investigators on Wednesday said chemicals stored in a CSX train that exploded and caught fire outside Baltimore are not a risk to nearly residents. Late Tuesday evening, firefighters responded to a fire and explosion at a derailed train site in Rosedale, Md., just outside Baltimore. They controlled the blaze shortly before midnight. At least one of the trains that had caught fire had been used to transport hazardous materials, and investigators were initially concerned about the risk to nearby residents, The Associated Press reported. They ruled within hours that the chemicals are not hazardous. Federal authorities are still looking for the reasons behind the fire. National Transportation Safety Board's Robert Sumwalt said a truck crossed the train tracks and collided with the derailed trains, but it still is not known why the driver was there. The driver, John Alban Jr., 50, was seriously injured in the crash and is still in the hospital recovering, AP reported.

Sen. Mazie Hirono (D-HI) appeared on CNN's "New Day" on Thursday. She commented on the news that Iran shot down an American drone in international waters. Hirono said there is a mistrust of the United States since President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Iran nuclear deal. "I think their perspective is 'how are we supposed to believe that the United States is going to keep its word?'" Hirono said. She added, "We need to create, I think, an environment where both sides, particularly at this point the Iranians believe that it is time to come to the negotiation table. Apparently, it's not that time yet. So, miscalculations can happen."

New Jersey Democratic Rep. Rob Andrews said Tuesday he is leaving Congress in two weeks. Andrews, who has held the Democratic-leaning suburban Philadelphia seat since 1990, will leave office February 18 to join a law firm with offices in Washington. He said the job just opened and he "had to make a decision this weekend." Andrews is the third congressional Democrat to resign in the past several weeks, starting with Rep. George Miller in January and Rep. Henry Waxman last week. Both are from California. Andrews, 56, had been the subject of a House Ethics Committee investigation related to whether he used campaign money for trips to California, where his daughter had a singing and acting career. His departure will end the investigations. The seat will be open until the general election in November. Miller's departure had put Andrews in line to be the top Democrat on the House Education and Workforce Committee.

Kevin Nicholson, the Republican presidential candidate, said his family has a lot of love and support from other relatives but remains confident in his political views. He was not always a conservative but said his opinions changed after serving in the Marine Corps. "If you want to have your illusions ripped away as a young person, go to war, and you're going to learn a lot about yourself and a lot about the world," Nicholson said. The race is set to be one of the most expensive this cycle with Richard Uihlein giving $3.5 million to the Solutions for Wisconsin super PAC that endorsed Nicholson. Baldwin also has a war chest, raising $2.8 million in the last quarter of 2017, according to ABC News. President Trump won the blue-leaning state in a surprising victory in 2016, making it a top target for Republicans this year.

President Trump tweeted Friday he would nominate Texas Representative John Ratcliffe for director of national intelligence. Ratcliffe had previously been nominated for DNI earlier in the year. Trump tweeted: "I am pleased to announce the nomination of @RepRatcliffe (Congressman John Ratcliffe) to be Director of National Intelligence (DNI). Would have completed process earlier, but John wanted to wait until after IG Report was finished. John is an outstanding man of great talent!" The tweet also stated: "At a time when the Russians are interfering in our elections, we need a nonpartisan leader at the helm of the Intelligence Community who sees the world objectively and speaks truth to power, and unfortunately neither Acting Director Grenell nor Rep. Ratcliffe comes even close to that."

Former Vice President Joe Biden said in a video released by his campaign that he would not accept damaging information about an opponent if a foreign entity offered it. "I won't be part of any attempt to undermine our democracy or public confidence in our institutions," Biden stated. Biden has repeatedly claimed that several world leaders begged him to run for president against Trump. The campaign video features Trump's interview with ABC News in which he said he would probably accept the information and turn it over to the FBI. Biden spoke directly to the camera while at a desk. "Donald Trump doesn't think it matters if candidates accept damaging intel on their opponent from a foreign government. He's dead wrong," Biden said. Biden also said the pledge requires candidates to "use no disinformation in their campaigns or tolerate outside interference."

On Tuesday, Rep. John Lewis (D-GA) appeared on MSNBC's "Andrea Mitchell Reports" and called for impeachment proceedings to begin against President Donald Trump. Lewis said, "We tried every other path and used any other tool. We will any find the truth unless we use the power given to the House of Representatives and the House alone, to begin an official investigation as dictated by the Constitution." He continued, "The future of our democracy is at stake. There comes a time when you have to be moved by the spirit of history to take action to protect the integrity of our nation. I believe, I truly believe, the time to begin impeachment proceedings against this president has come. To delay or to do otherwise would betray the foundation of our democracy."

A plagiarism scandal caused Democrat John Walsh to drop out of his U.S. Senate race in Montana. Democrats have started an online petition to draft Academy Award-winning actor Jeff Bridges. In the petition, author Pratt Pratt wrote: "He has great recognition! Charisma! Brains!" She added that Bridges is known internationally "but he is also highly accessible." She noted that Bridges first bought a house in Montana four decades ago. Before the plagiarism, Republican Representative Steve Daines was almost certainly going to take the seat. He was 10 points ahead at the time of the incident. Bridges owns a home in Montana and has donated to Democrats but has never shown any kind of interest in electoral politics.

The Senate unanimously confirmed Lt. Gen. Paul Nakasone to lead the National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command on Tuesday. Nakasone was President Donald Trump's nominee to replace Navy Adm. Mike Rogers, who announced his retirement from the dual role in February. The Senate used a process called "hotline" for Nakasone's confirmation, which speeds up the voting process for a nominee considered non-controversial. Before taking over as director of the NSA and Cyber Command, Nakasone was head of U.S. Army Cyber Command. He previously served in positions at the NSA and Cyber Command and has been praised by both Democrats and Republicans for his experience in the field, The Hill reported. His new job will come with a fourth star, a promotion after the Trump administration put Cyber Command on the same level as Central Command.

David Hogg said he will work in an advisory role for the company to focus on school as the venture is happening. He outlined the company's brand identity, stating: "Union made in America to create good jobs that support American families. Have an emphasis on supporting progressive causes. Not attempt a white supremacist overthrow of the United States government. So you can sleep at night." He wrote in one of several tweets Thursday: "We will have the name announced soon but we need to get through the legal process of trademarking as so on." Hogg acknowledged the venture is aimed at ruining MyPillow and Mr. Lindell. He said: "Mike isn't going to know what hit him — this pillow fight is just getting started."

Former New York Gov. George Pataki, a former 2016 GOP presidential candidate, endorsed Sen. Marco Rubio (R-TX) on Tuesday during an interview on Fox News's America's Newsroom. Pataki said Rubio "has the leadership, he has the vision" to be President of the United States, as well as the ability "to understand what it takes to defend us from radical Islam." Pataki said Rubio's experience in the U.S. Senate as being able to lead and "bring us together." "I'm going to do everything I can to help Senator Rubio," Pataki told Fox News's Martha MacCallum. Pataki, asked about fellow GOP candidate Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX), said Cruz is "a valuable asset...in the U.S. Senate."

The FBI said early Sunday that a suspect killed by Phoenix police in a bank robbery attempt is believed to be the same man accused in the shooting death of one Mississippi police officer and the wounding of another. The statement came hours after Phoenix police shot and killed the man minutes after Saturday's bank robbery attempt. The FBI said in an email statement: "We believe that this suspect is the same individual who is responsible for the attempted bank robbery in Atlanta, the robbery of the BancorpSouth in Tupelo, Mississippi, the shooting of Officer Joseph Maher, and the murder of Officer Gale Stauffer." Phoenix police had no immediate comment when contacted early Sunday. The slain suspect's name has not been released. The officers were shot Monday. Stauffer died and was buried Friday. Maher reportedly was able to walk with some aid on Friday.

In March, Hillary Clinton compared Russian President Vladimir Putin's aggression towards Ukraine to that of Adolf Hitler before World War II. Putin responded on Tuesday. "It's better not to argue with women. But Ms. Clinton has never been too subtle in her statements," Putin said. "When people push boundaries too far, it's not because they are strong, but because they are weak. But maybe weakness is not the worst quality for a woman." Clinton is not the only one who made the remarks. In Canada, a Jewish woman told Prince Charles how she fled Poland during World War II when he told her, "Putin is doing just about the same as Hitler." Putin was referencing Russia's hostility and annexing Crimea from Ukraine. Putin said these remarks were not "royal behavior."

Former Vice President Joe Biden said the events in Charlottesville were an "epiphany" to him because he had never seen anything like it in his lifetime. Video of Biden's remarks on Thursday evening at a fundraiser in Philadelphia were obtained by The Associated Press from attendees. Biden announced earlier in the day that he was running for president and said President Donald Trump's "moral equivalence" between white supremacists and counterprotesters was a major motivating factor. Biden made frequent mention of Trump at the fundraiser, saying, "Every nation is held up by an invisible moral fabric, and it's being shredded, and our kids are listening." He said he hopes in a few years people will realize that the Trump era was "an aberration in American history" "because this is not who we are."

Republican Rep. Jason Chaffetz of Utah said Wednesday he needs immediate foot surgery and will be out of Washington for three to four weeks, missing a key vote on a spending bill to keep the government open. Chaffetz, who chairs the House Oversight Committee, announced he will not seek re-election. He said in an Instagram post Wednesday he needs surgery to remove screws and pins from a foot he shattered 12 years ago. Chaffetz posted X-ray images showing the 14 screws and a metal plate in his foot. He said he injured his foot during a fall from a ladder at his home. He said he was "sorry to miss the important work we are doing in Washington ... but medical emergencies are never convenient." Chaffetz, 50, has not announced his future plans, although he says he is considering private sector jobs. He is a possible candidate for Utah governor in 2020.

President Trump said Saturday he does not think North Korean leader Kim Jong Un will lash out in a way that disrupts the U.S. campaign season. Pyongyang has launched short-range missile launches and used bellicose language. "We'll see about North Korea. I'd be surprised if North Korea acted hostilely," Trump told White House reporters as he left for events in Florida. "I have a very good relationship with Kim Jong Un. I think we both want to keep it that way. He knows I have an election coming up. I don't think he wants to interfere with that." Trump has had a personal relationship with Kim. He met Kim last summer at the demilitarized zone that divides the Korean peninsula.

The White House says President Barack Obama and Secretary of State Hillary Rodham Clinton will give their first joint interview to the television news show "60 Minutes" and it will air Sunday. Clinton is soon to leave her post as secretary of state and is being mentioned as a possible presidential candidate for 2016. Obama and Clinton competed for the Democratic nomination for president in 2008, and their relationship has been watched closely ever since. It is not clear what questions the two will face in their joint interview.

Kansas Gov. Jeff Colyer's campaign has established a "voting integrity" telephone hotline. Colyer's campaign announced the hotline Thursday. Spokesman Kendall Marr said it had received "countless" reports of voters experiencing issues at the polls. Kobach is the state's chief elections officers and told reporters Wednesday that he knew of no reports of irregularities outside of a long delay in the reporting of results from the state's most populous county because of issues with its new machines. Colyer's campaign announced the hotline as election officials confirmed that a mistake shorted Colyer's vote total for another county in the state's results by 100 votes.

Anthony Weiner, a sitting U.S. Congressman and Democrat, joined Business Insider. In May 2011, Breitbart News reported that Weiner tweeted a picture of his crotch to a young woman who was not his wife. Weiner initially claimed his Twitter feed had been hacked. He then accused Breitbart News founder Andrew Breitbart of lying. Weiner later admitted he had lied about everything and resigned his Congressional seat. During the 2013 New York City mayoral race, Weiner received name recognition from outlets including the New York Times and Buzzfeed Politics. Early polls showed him leading the race. A new revelation that Weiner had sexted with another woman destroyed that campaign.

Ruth Bader Ginsburg was hospitalized for heart surgery. The court said in a statement that the coronary blockage was discovered after Justice Ginsburg experienced discomfort during routine exercise last night and was taken to the hospital. She is resting comfortably and expected to be discharged in the next 48 hours. Ginsburg has previously addressed talk of her possibly resigning, telling Elle Magazine earlier this year that if she stepped down this year, President Obama could not appoint anyone she would like to see on the court. She said: "[The Senate Democrats] took off the filibuster for lower federal court appointments, but it remains for this court. So anybody who thinks that if I step down, Obama could appoint someone like me, they're misguided. As long as I can do the job full steam … I think I'll recognize when the time comes that I can't any longer. But now I can."

The U.S. Department of Justice is talking with beer makers Anheuser-Busch InBev and Grupo Modelo about potentially resolving a legal challenge to their $20.1 billion deal. The beer companies and the government are asking the court for a stay of all litigation proceedings until March 19. There is no guarantee a resolution will be found. The Justice Department in January sued to block the combination, saying having one company controlling nearly half of all U.S. beer sales would stifle competition. The beer makers recently revised the terms of the acquisition, which would give more control of Modelo's U.S. beer brands to a wine company, Constellation Brands Inc., in a side deal. The government is weighing whether the revised terms of the deal resolve its concerns about market competition.

The Navy is searching for a sailor who went missing from the USS Nimitz in the Arabian Sea late Sunday, military officials said. The Nimitz reported a "man overboard" just before 7 p.m. local time after conducting a thorough search of the ship. The aircraft carrier USS Nimitz (CVN 68) and guided-missile cruiser USS Princeton (CG 59) are conducting search and rescue operations in the North Arabian Sea following reports of a missing U.S. Navy Sailor, Sept 6, the Navy's Fifth Fleet said in a Twitter post. The Sailor has been listed as Duty Status Whereabouts Unknown on board aircraft carrier USS Nimitz. The Sailor's name is being held in accordance with U.S. Navy policy.

On Friday, Kellyanne Conway, the campaign manager for Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump, appeared on ABC's "Good Morning America." She told co-host David Muir that Trump's line from a night earlier at a rally in Charlotte, North Carolina, about his regret for some of his past remarks was "all him." Conway said this should incentive for those criticizing him to "some recognition and some forgiveness." She said: "He was talking about anyone who feels offended by anything he said, and that's all him. You know, he took extra time yesterday going over that speech with a pen, so that was a decision he made. Those are his words. And I hope that everybody who has criticized him at some point, David, for being insensitive or for mocking someone at least shows some recognition and some forgiveness."

The National Archives plans on Friday to release 2,500 more pages of documents from former President Bill Clinton's White House. The documents released since February cover the Clinton administration's health care overhaul plan, Republicans' victories during the 1994 midterm elections, and other topics. The records set for release Friday are the third batch to be released from the Clinton Presidential Library in Little Rock, Ark. The records have shed more light on former first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton's role within the administration and her aides' attempts to shape her public image. The records are being scrutinized by reporters and others as the former secretary of state and U.S. senator contemplates a second presidential campaign. About 8,000 pages of records have been released so far, part of roughly 30,000 pages expected to be released by the National Archives in the coming weeks.

Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, a Nevada Democrat, filed cloture to bring his debt ceiling bill to the Senate floor for a vote. The Democratic leader failed to secure the 60 votes needed to pass the cloture measure. The Republican majority voted 50 to 49 for cloture. Senator Scott Brown of Massachusetts voted with the Democratic majority for cloture. Two Democrats voted with the minority: Joe Manchin of West Virginia and Ben Nelson of Nebraska. Independent Bernie Sanders, who caucuses with Democrats, also voted against the Reid bill. Senate Democratic leaders gathered in House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi's office after the cloture vote to discuss their next steps in the debt ceiling debate. Senator Reid told me as he entered Rep. Pelosi's office that he remains confident a resolution would happen by the August 2 due date.

Voters in Colorado and Washington voted to legalize marijuana on Tuesday, while voters in Oregon voted against a similar initiative. Measure 80 failed in Oregon, largely because female voters supported the initiative. Washington state voters legalized recreational use of marijuana. In Colorado, voters approved an initiative that would make it legal for those over 21 years of age to possess one ounce of marijuana. Colorado Governor John Hickenlooper (D) said while "voters have spoken and we have to respect their will," federal law still says marijuana is an illegal drug. "This will be a complicated process, but we intend to follow through," Hickenlooper stated. "That said, federal law still says marijuana is an illegal drug so don't break out the Cheetos or gold fish too quickly." Many Colorado residents expressed concerns that the initiative would turn Colorado into a magnet state for marijuana dealers.

The Taliban claimed the capture occurred in December during a night raid in Afghanistan. The International Assistance Security Force, led by the United States, issued confirmation of the capture. An official said the dog was British, not American, Fox News said. "We can confirm that a military working dog went missing following an ISAF mission in December 2013," IASF said, AP reported. "It is ISAF policy to defer identification to the appropriate national authorities." The dog is a small dog, reddish-brown in color. A video shows a Taliban militant with long hair parading it before the camera. In addition to the dog, the Taliban displayed various weaponry members said were confiscated during the same raid, AP reported. Working dogs in Afghanistan are frequently used by ISAF forces, particularly German Shepherds, Labradors and Spaniels.

President Trump's physician, Dr. Sean Conley, said Monday night that Mr. Trump's unannounced checkup at Walter Reed National Medical Center last weekend was "routine" and that the president did not have any "acute" health issues such as chest pains. Addressing speculation about the president's checkup, Dr. Conley said his visit Saturday to Walter Reed National Medical Center was "a routine, planned interim checkup as part of the regular primary preventative care he receives throughout the year." In a letter released by the White House, the doctor said: "The president has not had any chest pain, nor was he evaluated or treated for any urgent or acute issues. Specifically, he did not undergo any specialized cardiac or neurologic evaluations."

A Quinnipiac University poll released Thursday morning shows Democrat Terry McAuliffe leading Republican Ken Cuccinelli by 5 percentage points. Cuccinelli, the state's sitting attorney general, received 38 percent support and McAuliffe 43 percent. The survey shows the race remains tight but shows McAuliffe has gained on Cuccinelli. A March 27 survey showed McAuliffe with a 2-point lead. Peter Brown, assistant director of the Quinnipiac University Polling Institute, said: "The 17 percent of voters who say they are undecided will determine the Commonwealth's next governor. At this point, neither man seems to have much of an edge."

Democratic House Minority Leader Rep. Nancy Pelosi praised Bernie Sanders for voting against the Clinton administration's Defense of Marriage Act (DOMA), which defined marriage as one man and one woman. "Bernie Sanders was my colleague in the House," Pelosi said in a forum at George Washington University, noting that she has not endorsed anyone in the Democratic race. "We voted against DOMA, you know, against all of those things people are subjecting to scrutiny now. He's fabulous, and he has a very important tonic for the country and for the Democratic Party because he has ideas." Hillary Clinton has been criticized for her previous support for her husband's DOMA law. In a 2004 floor speech, then-senator Hillary Clinton defended the heterosexual definition of the "sacred bond" of marriage.

CNN and host Jake Tapper apologized for an on-screen banner that appeared during his show on Monday. Tapper said the on-screen phrase was "unacceptable" and "horrified" him. The vacationing Tapper responded to viewer comments with several Twitter posts explaining that, despite his absence, he was "furious" and his "staff has heard from me." The phrase appeared during a discussion among Jim Sciutto, subbing for Tapper on "The Lead," and two journalists about President-elect Donald Trump's support from the alt-right. The segment focused on white nationalist leader Richard Spencer, whose anti-Semitic declarations Sciutto characterized as "hate-filled garbage." The on-screen phrase during the segment stated, "Alt-Right Founder Questions if Jews are People." CNN issued a statement calling that caption "poor judgment and we very much regret it and apologize."

President Trump criticized former President Barack Obama on Sunday, calling him "grossly incompetent." Returning to the White House from a weekend at Camp David, Trump was asked by reporters about Obama's criticism that his administration had shown a lack of leadership during the coronavirus pandemic. "Look, he was an incompetent president," Trump said. "That's all I can say. Grossly incompetent." During online remarks Saturday for an event honoring students graduating from Historically Black Colleges and Universities, Obama said, "More than anything, this pandemic has fully, finally torn back the curtain on the idea that so many of the folks in charge know what they're doing. A lot of them aren't even pretending to be in charge."

The Republican National Committee unveiled a series of online postcards mocking President Obama's upcoming vacation at Martha's Vineyard. One postcard shows Obama riding a bicycle. Another shows Obama holding a bodyboard stating "Finding a wave in Martha's Vineyard is almost as hard as finding a job." Another shows Obama bowling with the caption "I hope I bowl higher than my approval rating." The RNC believes Obama should remain in Washington to focus on repairing the economy. White House Press Secretary Jay Carney defended Obama's vacation last week when he said "there is no such thing as a presidential vacation" and that Obama would continue to be briefed on the economy. President Obama announced Wednesday he would unveil his plan on the economy and job creation in early September. The president leaves the White House Thursday afternoon and returns from his vacation August 27.

U.S. officials and Afghan counterparts have reached a tentative security agreement that includes a letter written by President Obama admitting "mistakes" during the "War on Terror." The New York Times reported the idea of the letter was originally proposed to Afghan President Hamid Karzai by Secretary of State John Kerry. With the letter, the Afghan government agrees to allow the U.S. to conduct "raids on Afghan homes in certain circumstances, which had been an area of disagreement." Another area of disagreement concerns a provision that says "U.S. forces staying in Afghanistan beyond 2014 cannot be tried in local courts for any crimes they commit." If the tentative agreement is accepted by all parties involved, U.S. troops will have sole control over Bagram Air Field, north of Kabul, but will share facilities on eight Afghan-run bases throughout the country.

Secret Service man Timothy McCarthy, who took a bullet during the attempted assassination of President Ronald Reagan, said he hopes a federal judge is right that John Hinckley is no longer a threat and can be released to live with his mother. McCarthy, now the police chief of the Chicago suburb of Orland Park, said he was not notified of the judge's decision to allow Hinckley to go free. McCarthy noted he has never been asked for an opinion on whether Hinckley should be released. During the March 30, 1981 assassination attempt, the then 32-year-old McCarthy was shot in the right chest. He said he spent a little more than three months recuperating before returning to the president's security detail.

President Donald Trump said Friday that the United States was "cocked and loaded" to retaliate against Iran for downing an American drone. He canceled the missile strikes 10 minutes before they were scheduled to be executed after being told some 150 people could die. Trump tweeted Friday that the U.S. will never allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon. He said he is in no hurry to respond to the downing of the U.S. surveillance drone over the Strait of Hormuz. His statement was the latest indication that he does not want to escalate the clash with Tehran, but he did not rule out a future U.S. strike. He said U.S. economic sanctions are crippling the Iranian economy and more are being added. Iran claimed Friday it had issued several warnings before shooting down the drone over what it said was Iranian territory.

Michael Vines, a man involved in a car accident, was arrested for unlawful possession of a firearm. According to the Greenville Police Department, Vines allegedly tossed a loaded .38-caliber revolver into the grass. According to police, Vines is federally prohibited from possessing a gun. Vines has a large tattoo of a gun across his forehead. Firefighters on the scene witnessed Vines allegedly tossing the gun away and alerted police. Vines was charged with driving with a suspended license, driving too fast for conditions, and unlawful possession of a firearm. The Greenville police said the real weapon was placed in property and evidence. The car accident occurred just southwest of downtown Greenville, South Carolina.

President Obama said during a press conference Friday that he would save Russian President Vladimir Putin if he were drowning. ABC News reporter Jonathan Karl asked Obama the question during a press conference in South Korea. Obama replied, "I absolutely would save Mr. Putin if he were drowning." He added, "I'd like to think that if anybody's out there drowning, I'm going to save them." Obama said he was a good swimmer while growing up in Hawaii but was a little out of practice. Putin was asked a similar question during a question-and-answer event in Russia last week. Putin replied, "I don't think I have a close personal relationship with Obama. I think Obama is a courageous and good person, and he would for sure save me."

South Carolina Gov. Mark Sanford said he considered resigning as his extramarital affair became public but vows to remain in office. Sanford spoke to The Associated Press on Sunday outside his coastal home on Sullivans Island. Wearing khaki shorts and a t-shirt, he talked of his faith in God and said leaving office would be the easy way out. The governor admitted last week to a yearlong affair with a woman in Argentina. He and his wife say they will try to reconcile. Some lawmakers are calling for him to resign because he used public money to see the mistress during one trip, and because he was out of touch with his staff during his recent weeklong tryst. Sanford said he did not use public money for the recent trip.

On Thursday, MSNBC host Chris Matthews will interview President Obama at American University in Washington, D.C. Obama will answer questions from the student audience and submit some online. Obama recently held an off-the-record meeting with several MSNBC hosts at the White House following the rollout of HealthCare.gov, an interim nuclear deal with Iran, renewed calls for immigration reform, and new budget negotiations on the horizon. MSNBC's website stated: "Obama's interview with Matthews comes following the rocky rollout of HealthCare.gov, an interim nuclear deal with Iran, renewed calls for immigration reform, and with new budget negotiations on the horizon." The article also included the question: "Matthews will discuss a number of topics with Obama, including voter suppression, healthcare, political gridlock in D.C., growing dissatisfaction with the government and more."

A Twitter feed belonging to the gunman who killed nine people, including his sister, outside a Dayton, Ohio, bar over the weekend showed left-leaning tweets lamenting the 2016 election of President Trump. The gunman, 24, was killed by authorities during the gun incident. The account @iamthespookster did not bear the killer's name but showed selfies that resembled known photos of him. Twitter took the account down late Sunday, fueling speculation that it belonged to the gunman. The account stands in contrast to the account operated by a Texas man accused of a shooting massacre in El Paso on Saturday that claimed 22 lives. That 21-year-old suspect espoused anti-immigrant leanings, according to a manifesto authorities allege was his.

Iran's Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif wrote on Twitter late Friday that the U.S. move to call an emergency U.N. Security Council meeting on protests in the country marks another foreign policy blunder for the Trump administration. Zarif wrote that the Security Council "rebuffed the U.S.' naked attempt to hijack its mandate." He wrote that the majority emphasized the need to fully implement the nuclear deal and to refrain from interfering in the affairs of other countries. Zarif wrote: "Another FP (foreign policy) blunder for the Trump administration." U.S. President Donald Trump has voiced encouragement for anti-government demonstrations that have broken out in Iran. The U.S. called the U.N. meeting on Friday, portraying the protests that began last week as a human rights issue that could spill over into an international problem.

Among Republicans, Barbara Bush tops at 45 percent and Hillary Clinton at 36 percent. Among independents, Barbara Bush receives 28 percent of their votes, CNN reported. Among whites, Clinton receives 24 percent. Obama receives 58 percent of their favor, followed by Clinton at 30 percent. Among Hispanics and Latinos, Clinton tops at 45 percent compared to Obama's 29 percent. The poll, conducted April 23-27, involved 1,000 adults around the nation who were polled by telephone. The poll has a sampling error of plus or minus 3.1 percentage points.
